evidence: Cic. Tusc. 2.40: aniculae saepe inediam bīduum aut trīduum ferunt
terms.comment: The alternatives exclude each other, or the second replaces the first: “this or that, not both” (Lewis & Short). Repeated, aut … aut, either … or. After a negative Latin keeps aut or turns it into nec … nec: “I don’t drink wine or milk” is nec vīnum nec lac bibō.

evidence: Cato Agr. 88: maenam āridam vel ōvum dēmittitō
terms.comment: The choice is free, and either will do: “or, if you like”. Vel potius, or rather.

terms.grammar: enclitic conjunction, added to the second word
evidence: Cic. Phil. 14.16: duābus tribusve hōrīs (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ph. 3.3.21: nē quid plūs minusve faxit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A light vel, mostly between numbers and small words: plūs minusve, more or less.

evidence: Hor. S. 2.8.16–17: Albānum … sīve Falernum tē magis adpositīs dēlectat, habēmus utrumque
terms.comment: “Or if”: in a condition, a second possibility; also a second name for the same thing, “or rather”. For “whether … or” see that record.

terms.grammar: conjunction, in direct and indirect questions
evidence: Plin. Ep. 2.8.1: studēs an piscāris an vēnāris an simul omnia?
terms.comment: The “or” of a question that offers a choice: Vīnum an aquam?, wine or water?

phrases.latin: aniculae saepe inediam bīduum aut trīduum ferunt
phrases.english: little old women often go without food for two or three days

phrases.latin: cavētō, quom ventus siet aut imber, effodiās aut ferās
phrases.english: take care not to dig up or carry a tree when there is wind or rain

phrases.latin: maenam āridam vel ōvum dēmittitō; sī natābit, ea muriēs erit
phrases.english: drop in a dried sprat or an egg; if it floats, that will be brine

phrases.latin: Albānum … sīve Falernum tē magis adpositīs dēlectat, habēmus utrumque
phrases.english: if Alban or Falernian pleases you more than what is served, we have both

phrases.latin: studēs an piscāris an vēnāris an simul omnia?
phrases.english: are you studying, or fishing, or hunting, or all at once?
